Abstract. Ambiguous medical image segmentation aims to provide a
series of diverse but plausible segmentation hypotheses. However, ex-
isting methods introduce stochasticity in a fixed and pre-defined man-
ner, failing to form a progressive semantic modeling process. To ad-
dress these challenges, we propose KANResDif to learn local resid-
ual difusion with Kolmogorov-Arnold Network, thereby assigning dis-
tinct roles across stages for ambiguity modeling. Specifically, we pro-
pose Independent Time Encoding that ofers spline-based time embed-
dings instead of linear ones from MLPs, which enhances the indepen-
dence across inference stages and assigns progressive semantic roles to
diferent stages. We propose Residual Schrödinger Bridge that injects
deterministic residual prior with learnable weights by constructing lo-
cal Schrödinger Bridge instead of following manually settings, achiev-
ing a flexible deterministic–stochastic interaction and stage-aware am-
biguity modeling thanks to local optimal difusion path. Extensive ex-
perimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that KANResD-
if achieves SOTA performance on GED and HM-IoU, with maximum
improvements of 16.8% and 7.7%, respectively, while maintaining com-
petitive performance on the MDM metric. Source code is available at
https://github.com/PerceptionComputingLab/KANResDiff.

· Kolmogorov-Arnold Network · Schrödinger Bridge.

1 Introduction
Ambiguous medical image segmentation (AMIS), aiming to generate a series of
diverse yet anatomically consistent predictions that reflect the underlying an-
notation distribution [13,18], relies on the explicit introduction of stochasticity
during inference to capture the inherent variability in clinical annotations. By ex-
ploring multiple anatomically consistent solutions, stochastic inference provides
a more reliable and comprehensive basis for clinical decision-making, improving
robustness against ambiguous boundaries and inter-observer variability [10,16].

areas such as classification, regression and image super-resolution.

localized function representations to reduce cross-stage interference during dif-

– We propose KANResDif to learn local residual difusion, the first paradigm
that enables dynamic and progressive stochastic modeling for ambiguous

– The proposed ITE introduces a novel time-embedding reparameterization
strategy based on locally supported basis functions, which significantly en-
hances the independence across diferent timesteps and facilitates a progres-
sive ambiguity modeling process.
The proposed RSB introduces a novel residual guidance mechanism by con-
structing a local Schrödinger Bridge, which dynamically regulates the con-
tribution of residual deterministic components, thereby enabling flexible and
adaptive determinism injection into the difusion process for AMIS.
– Experimental results on the LIDC dataset and ISIC subset demonstrate that

Coordination with Stochastic Difusion Models.
The proposed Residual Schrödinger Bridge (RSB) assigns dynamic weights in-
stead of manually predefined weights to residual components by constructing
local Schrödinger Bridges across inference stages, thereby achieving the least
costly difusion process and forming a flexible determinism coordination with
stochastic difusion models. Deterministic residual prior is significant in ambigu-
ous medical image as a constraint of overall plausibility. Traditional residual
difusion models introduce residual components into inference via fixed formula-
tion as eq. 6 without maintaining the true anatomy of difusion paths in latent
space, failing to preserve the semantic plausibility modeling [13,15].

To address the limitations, we optimize the difusion path for AMIS by

spans.content: 2.2 Residual Schrödinger Bridge Forms a Flexible Determinism
Coordination with Stochastic Difusion Models.
The proposed Residual Schrödinger Bridge (RSB) assigns dynamic weights in-
stead of manually predefined weights to residual components by constructing
local Schrödinger Bridges across inference stages, thereby achieving the least
costly difusion process and forming a flexible determinism coordination with
stochastic difusion models. Deterministic residual prior is significant in ambigu-
ous medical image as a constraint of overall plausibility. Traditional residual
difusion models introduce residual components into inference via fixed formula-
tion as eq. 6 without maintaining the true anatomy of difusion paths in latent
space, failing to preserve the semantic plausibility modeling [13,15].

x _ { t } = \sqrt { ( \bar { \alpha } _ { t } ) } \times x _ { 0 } + ( 1 - \sqrt { ( \bar { \alpha } _ { t } ) } ) \times f _ { \phi } ( X ) + \sqrt { 1 - \bar { \alpha } _ { t } } \times \epsilon\tag{6}
To address the limitations, we optimize the difusion path for AMIS by
constructing Schrödinger Bridges across inference stages and regarding resid-
ual components as additional refinement to original stochastic difusion path.
Specifically, ambiguity-aware inference procedure of the proposed RSB is:

x _ { t } = \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { n } \frac { \sqrt { \bar { \alpha _ { t } } } } { n } \times x _ { 0 i } + h _ { \mathrm { R S B } } ( t ) \times f _ { \phi } ( X ) + \sqrt { 1 - \bar { \alpha _ { t } } } \times \epsilon\tag{7}
where
h _ { \mathrm { R S B } } ( t )
is the dynamic weight at timestep t, serving both the refinement
of original difusion path to construct a Schrödinger Bridge and a flexible de-
terminism injection maintaining overall plausibility. n denotes the number of
plausible predictions, making the proposed RSB an AMIS-efective approach.
To form a Schrödinger Bridge, the inference procedure in eq. 7 should follow
SB-formed forward and backward PDEs as eq. 8 and 9, where the residual term
h _ { \mathrm { R S B } } ( t ) \times f _ { \phi } ( X )
serves as the control drift for minimum cost optimization:

\mathrm { d } X _ { t } = \Big ( \sqrt { ( \bar { \alpha } _ { t } ) } X _ { t } + h _ { \mathrm { R S B } } ( t ) f _ { \phi } ( X ) + \beta ( t ) \nabla _ { x } \log \varPsi ( X _ { t } , t ) \Big ) \mathrm { d } t + \sqrt { \beta ( t ) } \mathrm { d } W _ { t }\tag{8}

Forward Procedure: For the forward procedure, we aim to achieve a Schrödinger
Bridge difusion path. Therefore,
h _ { \mathrm { R S B } } ( t )
is optimized to matching the control
drift to the SB correction term:
